text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Top U.S. commander for region says U.S. force structure in Asia-Pacific, including possible cutbacks if Koreas reconcile, under scrutiny as part of major strategy review.
- Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Tony Tan says Singapore should learn from Switzerland's woes.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong files third lawsuit against Tang Liang Hong over remarks made in an interview published in the Straits Times on January 11.
- Former premier Nawaz Sharif defeats Benazir Bhutto with landslide victory in parliamentary elections.
- Government of Singapore Investment Corproation joins forces with Hong Kong-listed HKR International to take up stake in consortium which clinched a Singapore $1.6 billion Tokyo land parcel.
- Creative Technology shares take big tumble after Monday's gains and IPC Corp continues to be bugged by Korea woes.
- Healthcare group Parkway Holdings is making major thrust into India through joint venture with India's industrial and telecommunications groups, Escorts Ltd.
- Festive rush to buy cars goes into high gear.
- About 5,000 non-Chinese allowed to apply for British passports following remarkable climbdown by the U.K. government.
- Supreme Court judge in Mauritius authorises judicial mortgage value of U.S. $32.68 million to Amcol Holdings on property owned by ex-partner Roland Maurel's holding company.
- Listed UIC group keen to buy sizeable stake in listed as well as non-listed Thai property companies.
- Parkway Holdings to list its Indonesian healthcare operations on Surabaya Stock Exchange through initial public offer of 47 million new shares.
